questions.problem:
Calculate the minor of the entry ${d}_{33}$ in the matrix
$D=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & -1 & 54 \\ 11 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${d}_{33}=7$ (third row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $7$ are removed: 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & ∗ \\ 4 & -1 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${d}_{33}=7$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 4 \\  & =-3-(-8) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

find the minor ${M}_{12}$ of the element ${a}_{12}.$

${M}_{12}=${{field-1}}

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 3 & ∗ \\ 2 & ∗ & z \\ 1 & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${a}_{12}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{12} & =det[\begin{aligned}2 & z \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & z \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 5-z\cdot 1 \\  & =10-z\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
What is the minor of ${e}_{13}$ in the matrix
$E=[\begin{aligned}x & 2 & y \\ w-1 & 1-w & 3 \\ 1-w & w-1 & -10y\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the first row and the third column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & y \\ w-1 & 1-w & ∗ \\ 1-w & w-1 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}w-1 & 1-w \\ 1-w & w-1\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}w-1 & 1-w \\ 1-w & w-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(w-1)\cdot (w-1)-(1-w)\cdot (1-w) \\  & =(w-1)^{2}-(1-w)^{2} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

So, the minor of ${b}_{23}$ is

$$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${a}_{32}$ is $-50$, find all the possible values of $x$ in the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ x & 1 & 3x \\ -12 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and second column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & ∗ & 4 \\ x & ∗ & 3x \\ ∗ & -4 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${a}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 \\ x & 3x\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 \\ x & 3x\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-7)\cdot 3x-x\cdot 4 \\  & =-21x-4x \\  & =-25x.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${a}_{32}$ is $-50$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-25x & =-50 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=2.$

Given that the minor of ${a}_{11}$ is $17$, find all the possible values of $p$ in the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & p & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & p\end{aligned}].
$$

In **ascending order**, the values of $p$ are

$p=$ 
{{field-1}} $\,$ and $\,p=$

questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate the minor of ${a}_{11},$ we remove the first row and first column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & p & 4 \\ ∗ & -2 & p\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${a}_{11}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}p & 4 \\ -2 & p\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}p & 4 \\ -2 & p\end{aligned}| \\  & =p\cdot p-4\cdot (-2) \\  & ={p}^{2}+8.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${a}_{11}$ is $17$, so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}+8 & =17 \\ {p}^{2}-9 & =0 \\ (p-3)(p+3) & =0.\end{aligned}

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $p=-3$ and $p=3.$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${c}_{23}$ is $-86$, find all the possible values of $x$ in the matrix

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & -4 & 5 \\ 11 & x & 6\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 11 & x & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${c}_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 \\ 11 & x\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 \\ 11 & x\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot x-7\cdot 11 \\  & =-3x-77.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${c}_{23}$ is $-86$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x-77 & =-86 \\ -3x & =-9 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}

Therefore, the solution is $x=3.$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${r}_{33}$ is $3$, find all the possible values of $z$ in the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}z & -3 & -1 \\ 5 & z-8 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 6z\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and third column:

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}z & -3 & ∗ \\ -5 & z-8 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 6z\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${r}_{33}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}z & -3 \\ 5 & z-8\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}z & -3 \\ 5 & z-8\end{aligned}| \\  & =z\cdot (z-8)-(-3)\cdot 5 \\  & ={z}^{2}-8z+15.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${r}_{33}$ is $3$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}-8z+15 & =3 \\ {z}^{2}-8z+12 & =0 \\ (z-2)(z-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $z=2$ and $z=6.$

Calculate the minor of the entry $b_{21}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}10 & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & 8 \\ 4 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The minor of $b_{21} = 3$ (second row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $3$ are removed: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $b_{21}=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 2-5\cdot 7 \\  & =2-35 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & 0 & -3y \\ 1 & x+2y & 4 \\ -y & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & ∗ & -3y \\ ∗ & x+2y & ∗ \\ -y & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]

$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2 & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$
